posts.text: This is a great write up. It comes across so clearly that anthropic does NOT understand the “trust us, we’re the good guys” strategy is bound to fail at some point. They have a relatively narrow distribution of ideas and they’re racing toward the inevitable blind spot.
posts.quoted: Anthropic doesn't see itself as a "normal company." Dario Amodei believes both that 1) superintelligent AI could destroy humanity, and 2) our only chance at survival is to have his trillion-dollar tech company build it first. This is not an intuitive way to think about either

posts.author: natolambert
posts.name: Nathan Lambert
posts.text: The best part: anthropic employees are likely the only people who will read this and not understand the critique.

posts.author: natolambert

posts.text: I don’t agree with these statements. many public evals shift the Overton window to interesting new things. Then they are goodhart’d and private ones take over. Where you are in the cycle is important.
posts.quoted: if the eval is public, it's bad. all good evals are private

posts.author: natolambert
posts.name: Nathan Lambert
posts.text: I didn’t sign it, but I considered it. I do think Anthropic is power seeking and very effective at mobilizing its beliefs (which comes with risks they don’t do a good job acknowledging), but I found this statement too strong for my taste.
posts.quoted: Ahead of Anthropic’s IPO, a rare coalition across AI safety, open source, e/acc, science, and law has signed the MisAnthropic Statement. Read the statement or sign at: https:// misanthropicstatement.com

posts.author: natolambert
posts.name: Nathan Lambert
posts.text: I think it’s good for the ai safety community to strongly say anthropic isn’t the only one to listen to or trust.

This is stupid. What counts as a chinese model? 
What about Thinky's model distilled from Kimi?
What about composer, continued pretraining?
What about Nemotron, using tons of DeepSeek synthetic data?
What about that silly nous finetune for "american" values?
